findings.title: typecheck silently falls back to plain `tsc --noEmit` for Vue projects, so type errors in .vue files report clean
findings.evidence: cli/verify-helpers.js:21-28: with no typecheck/type-check/check-types/tsc script and a tsconfig.json present, it returns 'npx tsc --noEmit'. It never checks for vue or vue-tsc in deps. tsc ignores .vue SFCs. Repro project with src/Comp.vue containing `const count: number = "not a number"`: chemx typecheck --json returned {"success": true, "command": "npx tsc --noEmit", "errorCount": 0}, while `npx vue-tsc --noEmit` printed `src/Comp.vue(2,7): error TS2322 ... exit=2`. Use the local binary (node_modules/.bin) instead of npx so a missing typescript fails loudly and does not install the unrelated `tsc` npm package. Add the 8GB NODE_OPTIONS only when the project asks for it, or let the user set it through .chemxrc.

In chemx-review/vueproj (deps: vue, Comp.vue with `const count: number = "not a number"`), `chemx typecheck --json` returned success:true, command 'npx tsc --noEmit', errorCount 0, exit 0. `npx vue-tsc --noEmit` printed 'src/Comp.vue(2,7): error TS2322' with exit 2. findings.title: `cx do` / `chemx do` stops at the first verification command and exits 0, so later checks are silently skipped

Scratch project with test script `echo FAILING; exit 1`: `chemx do "typecheck" "test"` printed only `--- cx typecheck --- ✔ TypeScript typecheck clean` and exited with batch exit=0. Running `chemx test` alone in the same project exits 1. CLAUDE.md advertises `cx do` (batch) as the token-saving way to chain commands, and help line 150 gives the example `cx do "d" "p -s" "verify"`.

findings.title: Wrapped commands inherit the MCP server's stdin and have no timeout, so a child can read JSON-RPC frames meant for the server or hang the call
findings.evidence: cli/build/executor.js:11-16 calls spawn(command, { shell: true, stdio: ['inherit','pipe','pipe'] }) with no timeout. Under `chemx mcp`, fd 0 is the JSON-RPC pipe. Probe (scratch/mcp-stdin.mjs) started the real server, called chemx action=test with params.command `head -n 1 > stolen.txt`, then sent pings with ids 3-12. Result: `ids answered: [1,2,4,5,...,12]` and `stolen.txt: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"ping"}`. Request 3 was consumed by the child and never answered. In an earlier run with a single follow-up frame, the test call (id 2) blocked with no response. The same run also showed the test tool reporting success:true for a command that ran no tests.
findings.recommendation: Use stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe'] (or 'ignore' whenever not on a TTY) in executeBuild. Add a timeout (configurable, for example in .chemxrc, with a default around 15 min) that kills the process group (detached plus process.kill(-pid)) and reports `timedOut: true` instead of hanging forever.

verdict.note: executor.js:11-16 confirmed: stdio ['inherit','pipe','pipe'], FORCE_COLOR=1, no timeout. I re-ran mcp-stdin.mjs against my own scratch project. 'ids answered: [1,2,4,...,12]' and stolen.txt contained '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"ping"}', so the child consumed request 3. Downgraded to medium: the trigger here is a contrived stdin-reading custom command. Normal vitest, tsc and node --test runs under a non-TTY pipe do not read stdin. The missing timeout (MCP call hangs on a stuck child) is the more realistic risk.

findings.title: `chemx test <file> -t name` ignores -t, `-t=x` builds a broken command, and many target forms are silently dropped
findings.evidence: verify.js:168 only recognizes `--filter=`/`-t=`, and its regex `/^--(filter|t)=/` does not strip a single-dash `-t=`. verify.js:169 only accepts positional targets ending in .js/.ts or containing '/'. Host results: `-t guest` gave command `npx vitest run tests/unit/lock-screen-route.spec.ts`, 7/7 run (filter ignored). `-t=guest` gave `... -t "-t=guest"`, which vitest rejected (`Expected a single value for option -t`). `--filter=guest` worked (1 passed, 6 skipped). Scratch project: `chemx test b.spec` and `chemx test b.spec.mts` both became `npm run test` (full suite, 3 tests). The repo's own guard hook (.claude/hooks/chemx-guard.mjs:14-15) tells agents to use `chemx test [file] [-t name]`, which is the form that is ignored, and `chemx test --help` documents neither --filter nor targets. The MCP string form `test tests/a.spec.ts -t adds` does work, so CLI and MCP behave differently.
findings.recommendation: Use a real arg parser (node:util parseArgs) shared by the CLI and the MCP string form. Support `-t <name>`, `-t=<name>`, `--filter`, and any positional that is not a flag (pass through to the runner, which already filters by name). Reject unknown flags instead of silently dropping them. Document targets and filters in `chemx test --help` and list test/typecheck in `chemx help` (currently missing from the command list).

verdict.note: verify.js:168-169 match the description. In the vt project: `tests/a.spec.ts -t adds` ran 'npx vitest run tests/a.spec.ts' (filter dropped, 2 run). `-t=adds` built 'npx vitest run tests/a.spec.ts -t "-t=adds"' (0 total). `b.spec` became 'npm run test' (full suite, 3 tests). `--filter=adds` worked (1 passed, 1 skipped). .claude/hooks/chemx-guard.mjs:14-15 tells agents to use `chemx test [file] [-t name]`, which is the ignored form. findings.title: Runner detection prefers vitest over the project's actual test script and ignores sub-app or alternate configs in the monorepo
findings.evidence: verify-helpers.js:49-66: with a target or filter, any vitest dependency wins over a `node --test` script and the script's flags are dropped. Dogfood on the kit itself: `chemx test cli/verify.spec.js` became `npx vitest run cli/verify.spec.js` and failed 2/2 (false red), while `chemx test -- node --test cli/verify.spec.js` passed 16/16. Monorepo: from the host root, `chemx test apps/kitchen-synk/src/components/__tests__/empirical-stress.test.ts` ran `npx vitest run <file>` against the root vitest.config.js (include tests/**), which gave `No test files found`. Neither vitest.kitchen-synk.config.ts nor apps/kitchen-synk/vitest.config.ts is ever considered.
findings.recommendation: Derive the runner from the test script first (node --test, vitest, jest), then fall back to deps. When a target is given, walk up from the target to its nearest package.json or vitest config and run from there (or pass --config / --root). Allow `.chemxrc` to set test.command and test.targetCommand templates. When 'No test files found' happens, suggest the nearest config that does include the file.

verdict.note: In the kit, the test script is 'node --test cli/...spec.js' and devDeps include vitest ^5.0.3. `chemx test cli/verify.spec.js --json` produced command 'npx vitest run cli/verify.spec.js', failed 2/2 with 'No test suite found in file', success:false, a false red. verify-helpers.js:60-66 prefers vitest whenever a target is given. For the monorepo, apps/kitchen-synk/vitest.config.ts and vitest.kitchen-synk.config.ts exist and root vitest.config.js:10 includes only tests/**. I did not re-run the kitchen-synk case, but the code path makes the claim consistent. This JSON output also contained raw ANSI escapes, which supports the ANSI finding.

findings.title: ANSI codes are emitted when piped and also leak into JSON/MCP payloads
findings.evidence: cli/terminal.js:74 checks `process.stdout.isTTY === false`, but piped stdout has isTTY === undefined (`node -e 'console.log(String(process.stdout.isTTY))' | cat` gives undefined), so sanitizeOutputStreams never strips when piped (NO_COLOR=1 does work). Measured typecheck error output: 164 chars vs 113 with --no-color (+45%). executor.js:15 forces FORCE_COLOR=1 on every child, and failure details are copied raw: the -t= case JSON had 44 escape sequences, 2454 chars vs 2024 stripped (+21%), and MCP returns this verbatim. verify-helpers.js:92-101 parseTypecheckOutput also skips stripAnsi (unlike build/parser.js). With `"pretty": true` in tsconfig, chemx typecheck --json gave errorCount 0, errors [], and executionError full of \u001b[96m codes.
findings.recommendation: Use `!process.stdout.isTTY` (truthiness). Do not force FORCE_COLOR on children (set NO_COLOR=1 / FORCE_COLOR=0 unless --raw on a TTY). Run stripAnsi on every string that goes into a report (details, names, executionError) and in parseTypecheckOutput. For tsc/vue-tsc, add --pretty false to the auto-detected command.

verdict.note: terminal.js:74 checks `isTTY === false`, but piped stdout has isTTY undefined (confirmed: prints 'undefined'). `chemx typecheck | cat -v` shows ^[[38;2;... codes. Byte counts: 164 piped, 113 with --no-color or NO_COLOR=1. executor.js:15 forces FORCE_COLOR=1, and the JSON failure details carry escaped \u001b sequences (seen in the kit runner repro). Even a fixed stream-level stripAnsi would not remove those, because JSON.stringify has already escaped them. I did not re-test the pretty:true tsconfig sub-claim.

findings.title: Every failed user build prints a ~2.3KB prefilled GitHub issue URL to the chemx repo and writes .chemx/issues/*.md
findings.evidence: cli/build.js:57-75: any non-JSON CLI build with exitCode!=0 calls handleError. The output for `chemx build -- 'node -e "process.kill(process.pid,\"SIGKILL\")"'` ended with `Command Failed: ...` and `Prepped Issue: https://github.com/Chemical-X-Protocol/starter-kit/issues/new?title=%5BChemX+Failure%5D...` (one URL-encoded line of about 2,300 chars, including the working directory and stack paths). It also wrote .chemx/issues/issue-<ts>.md plus last-error-issue.md for each run (4 files after 4 failing runs). A user's own build failing is not a chemx bug, so this misattributes the failure, spends tokens, and leaves clutter in the project.
findings.recommendation: Only invoke the issue catcher for chemx-internal exceptions, not for a wrapped command exiting non-zero. Keep --prep-issue / --post-issue as explicit opt-ins. Never print the full encoded URL by default; print the local report path at most.

verdict.note: In a scratch project, `NO_COLOR=1 chemx build -- false` (exit 1) produced 2196 bytes of output. The longest line was a 1750-char URL-encoded GitHub issue URL with labels=chemx-failure,bug, ending with a local report path. It created .chemx/issues/issue-<ts>.md and last-error-issue.md. The claimed ~2.3KB size is in the right range.

findings.title: typecheck/test JSON (the MCP payload) can be several times larger than the raw tool output
findings.evidence: Host `chemx typecheck --json` (vue-tsc, 7 errors) was 2219 chars pretty-printed, 1669 minified as MCP sends it, against 586 chars for the equivalent raw `file(l,c): error TSxxxx: msg` lines (2.8-3.8x). 525 chars of that are per-error boilerplate: category TYPE_ERROR, severity ERROR, and suggestion 'Review TypeScript compiler diagnostic.' repeated. `chemx test --help` says '--json Output test summary as minified JSON', but verify.js:112/231 pretty-print with indent 2. findings.recommendation: Emit compact rows such as `errors: [["file",line,col,"TS1005","msg"]]` or group by file. Drop category/severity when constant and drop generic suggestions. Cap at N with a count of the rest. Minify --json as the help says. Group lint/typecheck by code or rule with counts (for example 393 of 415 lint errors are auto-fixable vue formatting rules), which tells an agent more than the first 10 rows.

verdict.note: The earlier host run's tc.json (pnpm run type-check, 277s, 4.4GB RSS) has 7 errors. It is 2220 bytes pretty, and 1669 bytes as JSON.stringify output, against 586 bytes rebuilt as tsc-style lines. Each entry repeats category TYPE_ERROR, severity ERROR and suggestion 'Review TypeScript compiler diagnostic.' Help text verify.js:152 says 'minified JSON', but line 231 uses JSON.stringify(report, null, 2).

findings.title: verify runs every step serially with no progress or per-step timeout; on the host it printed only its banner for 10 minutes
findings.evidence: verify.js:343-353 runs audit, then await typecheck, then await test, then build, sequentially. On the host, `timeout 600 chemx verify` gave exit=124 with only `⚡ Chemical X: Token-Conserving Project Verification` printed (84 bytes). Measured parts: typecheck alone 277s (vue-tsc, 4.4GB RSS) and test alone about 67s, so the remaining time went to the whole-monorepo AST audit. verify also has no lint step, and the MCP DISPATCHER has no `lint` action (`Unknown Chemical X action: "lint"`).
findings.recommendation: Run typecheck and tests concurrently (Promise.all; they are independent), stream a single status line per finished step to stderr, honor a per-step timeout, and report partial results if one step times out. 'two' : 'three' }}` and `:class` nested ternaries. `chemx check` returned `{"isClean":true,...}` and printed '✔ Crystalline: src/x/tpl-ternary.vue (0 hazards)', exit 0. findings.title: A status or dashboard read can delete a lease that another process was just granted
findings.evidence: cli/team/team-db-lock-promotion.js:84-104: cleanExpiredLeases reads `SELECT * FROM file_leases`, then for each row runs `DELETE FROM file_leases WHERE file_path = ?`. The DELETE keys on path alone and doesn't recheck locked_by or expires_at. getFileLockStatus (team-db-locks.js:137) and getSwarmStatus (team-db.js:40) call it outside any transaction, and the UI calls getSwarmStatus on every SSE refresh. Promote waiters only when the delete actually changed a row. Read paths should report expired leases as expired and leave the writes to the acquire and release paths.

findings.title: The CalVer scheme publishes every build as a semver prerelease, so caret/tilde ranges never match and `npm update` can't upgrade

findings.title: Backtrace and q outputs contain duplicate entries and misleading labels
findings.evidence: `chemx backtrace useBrandingStore` lists compass-dashboard.controller.ts three times and BrandingSettings.vue three times under 'Root Entry Points (15)', and chains 2 and 3 are identical. `chemx q useBrandingStore` labels files by their first export, not the match: `src/stores/branding.store.ts:390L (BrandingPluginConfig)` (the actual definition, not marked as such) and `src/routes/phone/composables/usePhone.ts:245L (AvailableAppInfo)`. findings.title: A literal ':memory:' directory containing a real .chemx/index.db exists in the kit root and is still being opened
findings.evidence: `ls -la ':memory:/.chemx'` shows index.db (282624 bytes, Sep 25), index.db-shm modified Oct 8 20:32, and index.db-wal. resolveIndexDbPath(cwd) (cli/search-schema.js:17-19) calls ensureChemxDir(cwd) unconditionally, so any caller passing ':memory:' as cwd, instead of using DatabaseSync(':memory:'), creates a directory with that name. Specs commonly use ':memory:' (e.g. cli/trend.spec.js:16), and the fresh shm suggests a test or tool still does this.
findings.recommendation: In openIndexDb, special-case cwd === ':memory:' (open in-memory and skip ensureChemxDir), add ':memory:' to .gitignore, delete the directory, and add a spec asserting that no ':memory:' path is created.

verdict.note: The directory exists: starter-kit/:memory:/.chemx contains index.db (282624 bytes, 2026-09-25), index.db-shm (modified 2026-10-08 20:39) and an empty -wal, so something still opens it. resolveIndexDbPath (search-schema.js:17-19) calls ensureChemxDir(cwd) unconditionally, as claimed. The suggested culprit is wrong: cli/trend.spec.js:16 uses `new DatabaseSync(':memory:')` correctly, and I found no `openIndexDb(':memory:')` caller, so the root cause is unidentified. The directory is already git-ignored via the .gitignore:3 `.chemx/` pattern, so it does not pollute commits.
